newsitem.title: UK: Major says no quick access to peace talks for IRA.
newsitem.headline: Major says no quick access to peace talks for IRA.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Saturday that the IRA cannot expect to "suddenly and cynically" declare a ceasefire and be admitted to peace talks on Northern Ireland in the near future.
Major, speaking outside his Downing Street office after a security alert forced the cancellation of the Grand National horse race, condemned the Irish Republican Army for wrecking the event.

There has been no claim of responsibility for the bomb alert that forced the cancellation of the 150th running of the Grand National and the evacuation of 60,000 racegoers, but Major said he had no doubt the IRA was to blame.

Major said it was quite possible that the IRA, which planted bombs on British motorway bridges on Thursday, would think it could now suddenly resume the ceasefire it abandoned in February 1996 and expect its political representatives to join peace talks on Northern Ireland.

"Well I hope they realise that they may think that way but the British government doesn't and the British people doesn't. And every time they behave in this fashion they put any chance of Sinn Fein re-entering the talks back further than it was before," Major said.
Britain has said it will not admit Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, to the Northern Ireland peace talks unless the IRA declares a lasting ceasefire.
